rationale: Tests that a complete electronics repair quote with a stated diagnostic result, part number, and warranty is not flagged into ambiguity.
quote_text:
Pinecrest Device Repair - Job 5521
Device: 14-inch laptop, model NX-4400, serial NX44-0099817
Received: 03 June. Diagnosed by: bench technician T. Aluru.

Customer complaint: screen shows vertical coloured lines across the left third of the
display; image otherwise intact.

Diagnostic result: external monitor output over HDMI is clean at 1080p, which places
the fault in the panel or its ribbon connector rather than the graphics chip. Ribbon
reseated on the bench, lines persisted. Panel confirmed faulty.

Quoted repair:
  LCD panel assembly, 14" FHD matte, part N140HCA-EAC, 1 no.        Rs. 7,900
  Bench labour, panel replacement, 1 hour                           Rs. 1,200
  Data handling and post-repair display test                        included
                                                                    ---------
  Total                                                             Rs. 9,100

Panel carries a 6 month warranty covering dead pixels, backlight failure, and line
defects. Warranty excludes physical damage after collection.
Turnaround: 2 working days from approval, subject to panel stock (in stock as of today).
No charge if you decline the repair; the diagnostic was free.

should_identify: The diagnostic reasoning is shown: a clean external output rules out the graphics chip, and reseating the ribbon ruled out the connector.
The exact panel part number, warranty terms and exclusions, and turnaround are all stated.
There is no charge for declining, which is worth telling the customer.
must_not_invent: A doubt about the diagnosis. The quote shows its working; manufacturing suspicion here is unsupported inference.
A price judgment on Rs. 9,100 or on the panel cost.
semantic_expectations.notes: The electronics_repair clean case. Demo mode has no electronics keywords at all, so this quote falls through the stub's fallback path — the resulting failures are a real coverage gap in the Demo analyzer, documented in docs/CURRENT_STATE.md, not a defect in the case.
